title: Customer Service Skills
summary: Learn to listen, communicate clearly, handle complaints and difficult customers safely, protect customer data and measure satisfaction.
audience: Shop owners, sellers, tutors, job seekers, secondary and university students

lessons.title: Understanding needs, listening and clear communication

body.p: Customer service means helping people get what they came for, and treating them with respect while you do it. It matters in a market stall, a phone shop, a school office, a restaurant, a tutoring group or a WhatsApp business chat. Good service brings customers back and makes them tell friends. Bad service makes them leave quietly and warn others.

A customer's first words are not always the real need. A man says, 'This phone charger is useless.' The real need may be a working phone by tonight. A parent asks, 'How much are your lessons?' and may really be asking, 'Will my child pass, and can I afford this?'. Good service finds the real need by asking gentle questions and listening.

list: Practical needs: working product, correct size, delivery on the promised day.
Time needs: a quick answer, no long waiting without information.
Emotional needs: to feel respected, not ignored or blamed.
Information needs: clear price, how to pay, what happens next.
Give full attention. Put your phone down or stop other work. In a chat, do not answer three customers half-way.
Let the person finish before you reply.
Repeat in your own words: 'So the zip broke after one day and you need it fixed before Saturday. Is that right?'
Ask open questions: 'What happened?' and 'What would help most?'
Note details. Write names, order numbers and promises.

body.p: Use simple words, short sentences and the customer's language when you can. Avoid jargon. Give the answer first, then the reason. Confirm important points: price, date, place and next step. In writing, one message should have one main point.

Example: Esi sells fabrics in Takoradi. A customer asks, 'Do you have this in blue?'. Esi could reply 'No.' Instead she writes: 'We do not have blue in this pattern right now. We have a similar pattern in blue, here is a photo, and the supplier can bring the same pattern in 4 days if you want to wait. Which do you prefer?'. She answered honestly, offered options and ended with a question.

steps: Stop and give attention.
Listen without interrupting.
Repeat the need in your own words.
Ask one open question if unclear.
Give the answer, then the next step.

body.tip: If you do not know the answer, say 'I will find out and tell you by 3 pm', then do it. This is better than guessing.

lessons.title: Tone in writing, chats and calls

body.p: Tone is how your message sounds: warm, rude, rushed, calm. On a call, people hear your voice. In chat, they only see words, so they cannot see your smile. The same sentence can feel kind or cold depending on tone.

list: Greet and use the name: 'Good morning, Kofi.'
Be polite but plain: please, thank you, sorry.
Avoid ALL CAPITALS, which looks like shouting, and avoid too many exclamation marks or emojis when someone is upset.
Do not answer with one word such as 'No' or 'Ok'. Add what you can do.
Check spelling and numbers before sending. Wrong prices cause disputes.
Reply within the time you promise, or send a short holding message such as 'I have received your message and will reply within one hour'.

body.p: Compare two replies to a late delivery question. Cold: 'Wait. Rider is coming.' Warm: 'Thank you for your patience, Ngozi. Your rider is 20 minutes away. I will message you when he arrives.' The facts are the same, but the second shows respect.

list: Answer clearly: 'Good afternoon, Bright Phones, this is Musa. How can I help?'
Smile while speaking. People can hear it.
Speak slowly enough and ask permission before putting someone on hold.
Do not eat or chat with others while on a call.
End by repeating the next step: 'I will call you tomorrow at 10 am.'

body.p: Voice notes are common in WhatsApp-style business. Keep them short, speak calmly, and send a text summary of prices and dates so there is a written record. Use the language the customer is comfortable with. If you are not fluent in it, keep sentences simple rather than guessing difficult words.

Example: Sam runs a phone-repair shop in Nairobi. A customer writes angrily: 'YOU HAVE HAD MY PHONE FOR 3 DAYS!!!'. Sam does not copy the tone. He replies: 'I am sorry for the wait, Peter. Your phone needed a part that arrived this morning. It will be ready by 5 pm today and I will message you when it is done.' The anger reduces because the customer sees an answer and a time.

steps: Read your message as if you were the customer.
Remove anything that sounds rude or blaming.
Add the next step and the time.
Send, then do exactly what you promised.

body.tip: Before replying to an angry message, take one slow breath and wait ten seconds. You will choose better words.

lessons.title: Handling complaints: acknowledge, apologise, solve, follow up

body.p: A complaint is information. It tells you what to fix, and many unhappy customers say nothing and simply leave. A customer who complains and is handled well can become more loyal than one who never had a problem. Use four steps every time.

steps: Acknowledge: let the customer finish and show you understand. 'I understand the shoes came with a broken strap.'
Apologise: say sorry sincerely for the experience, without excuses or blaming others. 'I am sorry this happened.'
Solve: offer a fix. Repair, replace, refund, discount or a clear alternative. Ask what they would like if there are several options.
Follow up: check later that the problem is truly solved, and fix the cause so it does not happen again.

list: Arguing, 'You must have broken it yourself.' Even if it may be true, ask neutral questions instead.
Blaming a colleague or a supplier in front of the customer.
Promising what you cannot do just to end the call.
Disappearing after the first reply.

body.p: Example: Grace, a seamstress in Freetown, delivers a dress that is too tight. The customer writes upset. Grace: 'Thank you for telling me, Aminata. I understand the dress is too tight at the waist and the event is on Saturday. I am sorry. Please bring it to me tomorrow morning and I will let it out free of charge, ready by 4 pm. I will message you at 4.' She acknowledged, apologised, solved with a time, and will follow up. She then checks her measurement notes to avoid repeating the error.

Decide in advance what you can offer without asking anyone, for example repair within 7 days or a replacement for a faulty item. Write it down. When staff know the limit, they can solve quickly. If a request is above your limit, explain you will ask your manager or owner and give a time to answer. Be fair: a policy should be consistent and honest, and respect consumer rights in your country, which in many places give customers a right to goods that match their description and work properly.

A small recovery gesture often matters more than a big gift: a sincere apology, quick action and a follow-up message. Keep a simple complaint log with date, issue, action and result, and look for patterns each month.

body.tip: Do not say 'calm down'. Say 'I want to fix this for you. Please tell me what happened.'

lessons.title: Saying no politely and dealing with difficult customers

body.p: Sometimes the answer must be no: an item is out of stock, a discount is not possible, the return period has ended, or the request is unsafe or against the law. A polite no keeps the relationship. A rude no loses it.

body.h: A polite no: reason, alternative, next step

list: Start with what you can do or an appreciation: 'Thank you for choosing us.'
Say no clearly and kindly, with a short true reason.
Offer an alternative: another date, a similar product, a partial solution.
End with a next step.

body.p: Example: A customer wants to return a hair product opened six weeks ago, but the shop's return period is 7 days and it is not faulty. The seller says: 'Thank you for telling me, Joy. I am sorry I cannot refund a product opened this long ago, because our return time is 7 days. If you think there is a fault I can ask the supplier to check it, or I can give you advice on how to use it. Which would you like?'. She is clear without being unkind. Faulty goods are different, so check consumer rules before refusing a refund for a real fault.

Most difficult customers are stressed, in a hurry or have been let down before. Stay calm, listen, and focus on the problem rather than the person. Lower your voice rather than raising it. If they insult you, say once: 'I want to help you, and I need us to speak respectfully.' If it continues, you may end the call or chat politely.

list: Never put yourself in physical danger for a sale. If someone threatens you or is violent, move away, call for help and involve the owner, security or police.
Do not meet strangers alone in a private place for a pick-up or payment. Choose a public place, take a friend or use a safe handover method.
Do not accept abuse that is discriminatory or sexual. You can stop the conversation and block the person. Tell your manager, family or a trusted adult.
Keep a record of threatening messages.

steps: Stay calm and listen.
Name the problem and what you can do.
Set one clear boundary if needed.
If safety is at risk, leave and get help.

body.tip: Say what you can do, not only what you cannot. People accept no better when they get an option.

lessons.title: Escalation, handling mistakes and keeping customer data private

body.p: Nobody solves everything alone. A good service person knows when to ask for help, how to own a mistake, and how to protect customers' private information.

list: The request is above your authority, such as a large refund.
The customer asks to speak to a manager or the owner.
There is a safety, legal or health issue.
You do not know the answer after trying.
The problem keeps repeating.

body.p: Escalate well. Tell the customer what is happening and the time: 'I am passing this to my manager, Mr Banda, who can approve this. He will call you today by 2 pm.' Give your manager the full story in writing so the customer does not repeat everything: name, order, what happened, what was tried, what the customer wants. Stay involved until it is resolved.

Everyone makes mistakes: wrong price, wrong item, missed appointment. Admit it quickly, apologise, fix it and tell the customer how you will stop it happening again. Hiding a mistake nearly always makes it worse. Example: a tutor in Dublin double-booked two students. She messaged both the same morning: 'I made a booking error. I am sorry. I can offer Tuesday at 4 pm or Wednesday at 5 pm, and the session is free this week.' Both students accepted.

Customers trust you with names, phone numbers, addresses, payment details, photos and sometimes health or school information. Treat these as private. Laws on personal data exist in many places, including the UK, Ireland, Spain, Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya, and the details differ, but the habits below are safe everywhere.

list: Collect only what you need. A phone number and delivery address are enough for a delivery.
Use it only for the reason given, and ask permission for anything else.
Do not share a customer's details, photos or orders with others, including in group chats.
Never post screenshots of chats that show names, numbers or payment details without hiding them.
Protect your phone with a lock, do not leave books of customer details open on the counter, and delete old data you no longer need.
Never ask for or send a customer's PIN or password. Be careful with payment confirmations and check that the money has really arrived before releasing goods.

steps: Decide what you can fix yourself.
Escalate early when you cannot, with a full written summary.
Tell the customer what happens next and when.
Protect their data at every step.

body.tip: Before sharing any customer information, ask: would this customer be happy to see where I am sending it?

body.p: You can feel that customers are happy, but numbers show whether it is true and whether it is improving. Measurement can be very simple: a short question after service and a notebook or spreadsheet.

list: Satisfaction rate: satisfied customers divided by customers asked, times 100.
Average rating: the sum of all ratings divided by the number of ratings.
Complaint rate: complaints divided by orders or customers served, times 100.
First-contact resolution: problems solved at the first contact divided by all problems, times 100.
Response time: how long customers wait for a first reply.
Net score: percent who would recommend you (promoters) minus percent who would not (detractors).

body.p: Example 1. You ask 60 customers if they were happy and 48 say yes. Satisfaction = 48 / 60 = 0.8 = 80%.
Example 2. 50 ratings out of 5: twenty 5s, fifteen 4s, ten 3s, three 2s and two 1s. Total = 100 + 60 + 30 + 6 + 2 = 198. Average = 198 / 50 = 3.96.
Example 3. A shop had 200 orders and 14 complaints. Complaint rate = 14 / 200 = 7%.
Example 4. Out of 40 problems, 25 were fixed in the first conversation. First-contact resolution = 25 / 40 = 62.5%.
Example 5. Of 100 customers asked if they would recommend you, 60 are promoters, 25 are neutral and 15 are detractors. Net score = 60% - 15% = 45.

Ask short questions at a good time, such as right after delivery: 'How was your experience, from 1 to 5? What one thing could we improve?'. Read the comments, not only the numbers. Small samples can mislead, so do not judge from 3 replies. Share results with your team, thank people for good service, choose one improvement a month and measure again. Never pressure or reward customers in a way that makes them give false ratings, and do not delete honest feedback.

steps: Choose two numbers to track.
Collect them every week in the same way.
Look for patterns in comments.
Make one change and measure again.

body.tip: Close the loop. Tell customers 'You said deliveries were late, so we now send tracking updates.' They will give feedback again.

quiz.q: A customer says, 'This charger is useless!' What is the best first response?
options: Offer a refund before they explain
Tell them chargers last only a short time
Say you sold hundreds with no problem
Ask what happened and what they need, and repeat it back to confirm

quiz.q: A customer asks for blue fabric you do not have. Which reply is best?
options: We do not have blue in this pattern. Here is a similar one, or we can order it in 4 days. Which do you prefer?
No, we do not have it.
Try another shop.
Maybe, come back often.

quiz.q: An angry customer writes in capital letters. Which reply has the best tone?
options: Your phone will be ready when it is ready.
PLEASE STOP SHOUTING, I AM TRYING TO HELP
I am sorry for the wait. The part arrived this morning and your phone will be ready by 5 pm. I will message you.
Okay.

quiz.q: What is the correct order for handling a complaint?
options: Solve, apologise, acknowledge, forget
Explain why it is not your fault, solve, close
Apologise, close, follow up, acknowledge
Acknowledge, apologise, solve, follow up

quiz.q: A dress is too tight and the event is on Saturday. The seamstress says, 'Bring it tomorrow morning, I will adjust it free and have it ready by 4 pm, and I will message you.' Which step of the four-step method does the message about 4 pm and the later message mainly show?
options: Saying no
Only acknowledge
Escalation
Solve and follow up

quiz.q: A customer wants to return a product opened six weeks ago. It is not faulty and your return period is 7 days. What is the best reply?
options: Explain kindly why you cannot refund, offer an alternative such as checking for a fault or advice, and ask which they prefer
Refuse and say nothing more
Give a full refund to avoid trouble
Argue that the customer is cheating

quiz.q: A customer insults you during a chat. What is the best action?
options: Insult them back
Say once that you want to help and need respectful language, and end the chat politely if it continues
Ignore the issue and agree with everything
Post the chat publicly with their name

quiz.q: A stranger asks you to bring a phone alone to a quiet place at night to collect payment. What should you do?
options: Go but keep quiet
Suggest a public place in daytime, bring a friend or use a safe method, and refuse if they insist on the unsafe plan
Go, because a sale is a sale
Send your home address to be safe

quiz.q: A customer asks for a refund much larger than you may approve. What is the best action?
options: Tell the customer you are passing it to the owner, give a time for an answer, and send the owner a full written summary
Ignore the message until they stop
Refuse immediately
Promise it and hope the owner agrees

quiz.q: You quoted the wrong price and the customer already paid the lower amount. What is the best response?
options: Hide it and hope they never notice
Admit the mistake, apologise, explain the options clearly and try to fix it fairly, then check your price list
Blame the customer for not checking
Cancel the order without explaining

quiz.q: A customer gives you a phone number and address for delivery. Which use of this information is right?
options: Use them to deliver the order and for anything else only if the customer agrees
Share them with a friend who also sells
Add them to a public group chat for advertising
Post a screenshot of the order with the number visible as proof

quiz.q: You ask 60 customers if they were satisfied and 48 say yes. What is the satisfaction rate?
Fifty ratings out of 5 are: twenty 5s, fifteen 4s, ten 3s, three 2s and two 1s. What is the average?
A shop had 200 orders and 14 complaints. Out of 40 problems, 25 were solved at first contact. Which pair of figures is correct?
options: Complaint rate 7%, first-contact resolution 37.5%
Complaint rate 14%, first-contact resolution 25%
Complaint rate 7%, first-contact resolution 62.5%
Complaint rate 28%, first-contact resolution 62.5%

quiz.q: Of 100 customers, 60 would recommend you, 25 are neutral and 15 would not recommend you. The net score is promoters minus detractors. What is it, and what is a sensible next step?
options: 85, so stop asking for feedback
45, so read the comments from the 15, fix common issues and measure again
60, because neutral customers do not count
45, so ask customers to change their scores
